recommendation: Keep the fixed commit as-is; it completes the published Jira decision in the current build without broadening delete semantics or requiring additional work-group review.
issue_request: FHIR-23996 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for FHIR-core-http. It requested that the HTTP page stop stating too strongly that deleted resources return 410, because policy environments may require treating deleted resources like resources that never existed, and it requested a link to the security Access Denied guidance.
initial_application: Commit 639dbcd2848776be444488fe66b23438c581256d partially applied the issue by adding the intended conditional 410 and Access Denied caveat to the delete interaction. The read note and vread paragraph were only updated to say 410 Gone/link to delete details, leaving the remaining unconditional/should-return wording in current source.
additional_context: source/http.html is an active top-level RESTful API page linked from source/documentation.html. The delete, delete-history, and delete-history-version sections already use conditional 410 and Access Denied language, and source/security.html explains that Access Denied responses are policy/context controlled and may use 404 to avoid data leakage. Direct FHIR-23996 Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Changed source/http.html in the read note and vread deleted-version paragraph to say 410 Gone can be returned when the server wishes to indicate deletion, while systems may treat deleted records as unknown or return another Access Denied response for policy/security reasons. The status-code summary table was left unchanged because it lists 410 as a possible response.
source_changes: source/http.html:652-656 now frames 410 Gone for read as conditional and links policy/security alternatives to Access Denied Response Handling.
source/http.html:703-705 now frames vread of a deleted version as conditional 410 Gone or another Access Denied response rather than a should-return 410 rule.
